title: Because Something Has to be Said
speaker: Marc Anderson
summary: Marc Anderson opens by explaining that Iroquois elders began gatherings with a Thanksgiving prayer so hearts start as one before disagreement arrives. Marc then traces the region's geological and human ancestors, from the Pacific Ring of Fire to the Salish Sea. Poems by Leonard Cohen and Nanao Sakaki alternate with Marc's own, and Marc plays the berimbau, which turns out to be tuned wrong after a bow switch. A fox woman story anchors the middle: a lonely hunter loses her when he complains of her belt's scent, and he mourns every season. Marc reads Sakaki's "Love Letter," whose widening circles end with sitting, praying, and singing.

In a forest ten kilometers large, gather firewood, water, wild vegetables, and amanitas. Mountainous country Shenandoah. One hundred kilometers large, where someone lives leisurely, they say. Within a circle one thousand kilometers large, go see the southern coral reefs. Or the winter drifting ices in the Sea of Akhatsk. Within a circle ten thousand kilometers large, walking somewhere on earth. Within a circle one hundred thousand kilometers large, swimming in the sea of shooting stars. Within a circle one million kilometers large, upon the spaced out yellow mustard blossoms.

The moon in the east, the sun west. Within a circle ten thousand light years large, the galaxy full blooming in spring. Within a circle one million light years large, Andromeda is melting away in snow and cherry flowers. You sit, pray, and sing. You sit, pray, and sing. You pray and sing.
